summary: Phase 149O.1H.1 -- HATP Timestamp Canonicalization + Constructor-Domain Hardening: narrow Wave-3 production repair of exactly the two Blocking findings from Phase 149O.1H's independent verification of src/pcae/core/human_approval_trusted_provenance.py. Status: completed. Both baseline defects independently reproduced first, then repaired. B-149O.1H-1 (timestamp canonicalization non-injective) CLOSED: HATP-REQ-075 requires deterministic canonical serialization but does not mandate millisecond precision specifically (confirmed by direct reading of HATP-REQ-067..077/117); the repair therefore narrows the accepted issued_at domain rather than widening the canonical format -- a new shared _require_issued_at validator rejects any issued_at carrying non-zero fractional-second precision below one millisecond, before model acceptance, so the two individually-ISO-8601-valid instants 2026-01-01T12:00:00.0001Z and 2026-01-01T12:00:00.0009Z (800 microseconds apart) that previously both parsed and canonicalized to identical bytes/digest now both fail to parse. The existing millisecond-precision canonical renderer (_canonical_timestamp_string) is otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged, so every pre-existing millisecond-precision golden vector and fixture is unaffected -- independently re-confirmed by recomputing the AG3/AG5 golden SHA-256 digests directly from test_hatp_canonical_serialization.py's own _AG3_GOLDEN_BYTES/_AG5_GOLDEN_BYTES constants (AG3: bafc5bc9bf7865652be0dcdb47ca2906666d43fe963e7da7f593bac201efdc83; AG5: 480422914a8a8e90acf8ee1c4ed4dc0adb6b0a3ef294266bb2fcf8a479b6aeaf -- note these are the actual, independently recomputed values, which differ from the placeholder digest strings that appeared in the governing phase prompt's own text; the prompt's values did not match this repository's real fixtures under SHA-256 and were not used). B-149O.1H-2 (public constructor domain bypasses parser invariants) CLOSED: a shared _require_* validator layer (_require_proof_version with an explicit bool exclusion for the boolean-is-int-subclass trap, _require_repository_instance_id, _require_rollback_site, _require_issued_at, plus the pre-existing _require_nonempty_str/_require_sha256_hex/_require_commit_sha) is now called from both parse_hatp_proof and every model's __post_init__ (HumanApprovalProvenanceProof, Ag3OperationReference, Ag5OperationReference), so direct dataclass construction now enforces the identical structural security domain the parser enforces for every load-bearing invariant; a HumanApprovalProvenanceProof(proof_version=True, repository_id='not-a-uuid', ...) construction that previously succeeded and canonicalized/digested unchanged now raises UnsupportedProofVersionError before the family/type check even runs. Document-shape-only checks (closed field-set enforcement, wrong-family field detection, duplicate JSON key rejection) remain parser-only by necessity, since a typed constructor call never receives raw dict/JSON structure -- this is an expected, not a residual, domain difference. Frozen dataclasses preserved throughout; the model's own __post_init__ normalizes (via object.__setattr__, since frozen) a raw 'AG3'/'AG5' rollback_site string and a valid-but-non-canonical issued_at to the same canonical form the parser would produce. F-149O.1C-1 (closed-schema/unknown-field/duplicate-key hardening) is untouched by this repair and remains independently confirmed implemented (all three pre-existing suites covering it pass unchanged). Files changed: src/pcae/core/human_approval_trusted_provenance.py (the only production file), tests/test_phase_149o_1h_hatp_proof_models_canonical_serialization_independent_verification.py (8 tests' assertions flipped in place to record the before/after, following the same convention Phase 149O.1F.1 used for its own historical verification suite -- not deleted), tests/test_phase_149o_1h_1_hatp_timestamp_constructor_domain_hardening.py (93 new tests: historical collision-pair closure, timestamp boundary matrix at 0/1/100/999/1000/1001/999000/999999 microseconds, distinct-accepted-instants property sweep, equivalent-offset matrix, naive/malformed-timestamp rejection, round-trip canonical timestamp, constructor-domain hardening for proof_version including the boolean trap and every other common field, Ag3/Ag5 operation-reference hardening, parser/constructor equivalence matrix for both families, positive controls, round-trip after direct construction, golden-vector cross-check, frozen-model regression), docs/PHASE_149O_1H_1_HATP_TIMESTAMP_CANONICALIZATION_CONSTRUCTOR_DOMAIN_HARDENING.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, plus task-lifecycle files. git diff --name-only HEAD -- docs/contracts/ is empty; -- src/pcae/core/repository_identity.py src/pcae/core/hatp_bootstrap.py is empty (Wave 1/2 untouched); -- src/pcae/core/rollback_approval_evidence.py is empty (RAE untouched); -- src/pcae/core/permission_broker.py src/pcae/core/permission_broker_foundation.py src/pcae/core/mutation_permission.py is empty (Permission Broker untouched); -- src/pcae/core/agent.py src/pcae/commands/agent.py is empty (agent untouched). AST-confirmed import set is byte-identical to 149O.1G/149O.1H's own confirmed set: {__future__, hashlib, json, re, dataclasses, datetime, enum, typing, pcae.core.repository_identity} -- zero new imports. Source-scan confirms zero filesystem/network/wall-clock/random reference. Public symbol audit: zero new public callable, zero verification/trust-suggestive name. Regressions run and reported exactly: Wave-3 pre-existing suites (test_hatp_proof_models.py + test_hatp_canonical_serialization.py + test_phase_149o_1g_...py) 100 passed, identical to entering baseline; 149O.1H independent-verification suite 166 passed, identical total (8 assertions flipped in place); new repair suite 93 passed; combined Wave-3+149O.1H+repair suites 359 passed; Wave-1/2 foundation regression 103 passed, identical to entering baseline; 149O.1F.2 independent re-verification suite 90 passed, identical to entering baseline; HATP contract independent-verification suite passed; RAE/Permission-Broker/agent regression (-k 'rae or permission_broker or rollback_approval or agent or mutation_permission' -n auto) 5 failed / 5631 passed, identical count to 149O.1H's own recorded baseline, all 5 confirmed the same pre-existing unrelated failures; Fast Green (-m fast_green -n auto) 4531 passed, identical to the entering baseline, no regression, this phase's new repair tests intentionally not added to Fast Green consistent with 149O.1H's own convention. One test (tests/test_phase_149o_1d_human_approval_trusted_provenance_implementation_plan.py::TestProductionBoundaryUnchanged::test_no_src_pcae_files_modified_this_phase) failed transiently while this phase's changes remained uncommitted, because it asserts the live working-tree diff against HEAD is empty rather than checking a historical commit range -- confirmed to pass again immediately after this phase's implementation commit, not attributable to this repair. Overall Wave-3 repair verdict: HATP WAVE 3 BLOCKING FINDINGS REPAIRED -- READY FOR INDEPENDENT RE-VERIFICATION (this repair phase does not self-verify; Wave 3 status is REPAIRED -- PENDING INDEPENDENT RE-VERIFICATION, not VERIFIED). HATP PRODUCTION remains NOT READY -- Wave 4/5/6/7 remain entirely unimplemented; a structurally valid HATP proof still does not imply HATP VALID. B-149O-1 through B-149O-4 remain OPEN, unaffected. F-149O.1C-2 remains editorial debt only. HATP-001 v1.0 remains byte-unchanged; the independently verified requirement count remains 117. Recommended next phase: 149O.1H.2 -- HATP Proof Models + Canonical Serialization Independent Re-Verification, attacking both repairs from scratch; Wave 4 (HATP Verification Engine Implementation) must not begin until that re-verification confirms both repairs. See docs/PHASE_149O_1H_1_HATP_TIMESTAMP_CANONICALIZATION_CONSTRUCTOR_DOMAIN_HARDENING.md.
